subject: weasel on electrical cable
title: What If a Weasel Shut Down the Biggest Machine on Earth? In 2016 One Did

scenes.text: What if a weasel shut down the biggest machine on Earth? In 2016, one did.
The Large Hadron Collider: a 17-mile ring of superconducting magnets under the Swiss-French border, a seven-billion-dollar machine that found the Higgs boson.
At 5:30 in the morning on April 29th, 2016, a weasel climbed into a 66,000-volt transformer and bit a power cable.
An electric arc, a short circuit, and the most powerful particle accelerator ever built went dark. The weasel did not survive.
Repairs took a few days. It wasn't even the first time: in November 2009 a bird dropped a piece of baguette into the electrics and shut it down too.
Thousands of physicists, decades of work, 17 miles of magnets. Beaten by a bird's breakfast and a hungry weasel.

description:
What if a weasel shut down the Large Hadron Collider? On 29 April 2016, one did.
At about 5:30 a.m. a weasel got into a 66 kV transformer at CERN and gnawed a power cable, causing an electrical arc and a short circuit that took the 17-mile, roughly 7-billion-dollar accelerator offline for a few days of repairs. The animal did not survive. It was not the first animal to stop the machine: in November 2009 a bird is believed to have dropped a piece of baguette into the electrical equipment, briefly shutting the collider down.
